issues.title: Mandatory account creation blocks booking completion

quote.text: I just want to pick a time, not sign up.

issues.why: Ben reached the account creation screen after selecting his service, date, and time, but abandoned the task because he was required to create a full account instead of being offered a guest checkout or login option. The 'Log in' link for existing users is visually weak and easy to miss, forcing new users through the entire registration form.

fix.summary: Add a guest checkout option and make the existing user login link prominent on the account creation screen.
fix.before: Users must fill out a full account creation form (first name, last name, email, mobile, date of birth, password, confirm password) and accept terms before they can confirm a booking. The 'Already have an account? Log in' link is embedded in a sentence and visually weak.
fix.after: Offer a 'Continue as guest' path that collects only essential contact details (name, email, phone) for the booking confirmation. Make the 'Log in' link a standalone button with clear visual weight so returning users can bypass the form.

issues.title: Afternoon time slots not visible until date is clicked

quote.text: I'll click Tue 27 to see if it moves the calendar forward.

issues.why: All five users had to click the Saturday 24 date button before any time slots for that day loaded. The calendar shows dates as unselected buttons with no indication of morning or afternoon availability, forcing users to click each date to discover if their target window exists. Amara clicked Tuesday 27 first, and Sofia initially selected a morning slot before realizing she needed an afternoon…

fix.summary: Show time-of-day availability indicators on date buttons or load afternoon slots for the next Saturday by default.
fix.before: Date buttons (e.g., 'Sat 24') display no time information. Users must click a date to reveal its time grid. The Continue button appears disabled until a time is selected.
fix.after: Add visual cues on date buttons such as 'AM only', 'PM available', or 'Full' so users can scan for afternoon availability without clicking. Alternatively, default the calendar to the next Saturday and pre-load its time grid.

issues.title: Service selection required before seeing any availability

quote.text: I'm not sure where to start - do I pick a date first or a person?

issues.why: Users must choose a service on S2 before they can view date and time availability on S3. Amara was confused about the sequence, and Ben wanted to see open times immediately. The flow forces a service commitment without knowing if the preferred Saturday afternoon slot is open, increasing the risk of backtracking.

fix.summary: Allow users to check date and time availability before committing to a service.
fix.before: Step 1 (SERVICE) is mandatory and locked. The progress indicator shows SERVICE as active with no confirmation of selection. No date or time picker exists on S2.
fix.after: Make the flow flexible: let users browse dates and times first, or show a combined view where service, date, and time can be selected in any order. Keep the service selection but do not gate the calendar behind it.

issues.title: Low contrast text on calendar and progress indicator

quote.text: Let me pick Saturday 24th for my appointment.

issues.why: The calendar shows disabled days (e.g., 'Sun 25 Closed', 'Mon 26 Closed') and time buttons at 2.9:1 contrast ratio, below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA threshold. The progress indicator text on S2 also measures 2.9:1. Elena and other users with lower digital confidence or vision impairments may struggle to distinguish available from unavailable slots.

fix.summary: Increase text contrast to meet WCAG 1.4.3 AA (4.5:1) for all calendar labels and progress step text.
fix.before: Disabled day labels and time buttons use low-contrast gray text measuring 2.9:1 against the background. Progress step numbers and labels on S2 also measure 2.9:1.
fix.after: .calendar-day.disabled, .time-slot.disabled, .progress-step { color: #595959; } /* example: darken text to achieve 4.5:1 on white */

issues.title: Identical 'Select' buttons with no service label on S2

quote.text: I choose the first service option for a haircut.

issues.why: All eight 'Select' buttons on the service page have identical visible text and no accessible name indicating which service they belong to. Sofia picked the first option by position. Screen reader users and non-native readers must rely on spatial memory or context to distinguish services.

fix.summary: Add the service name to each Select button's accessible label.
fix.before: Each service card shows the service name above a generic 'Select' button. The button has no aria-label or hidden text identifying its service.
fix.after: Set aria-label on each button to 'Select Signature Cut & Finish', 'Select Restyle Consultation', etc., matching the service title in its card.
